lesson.title: Mi Amigo, Mi Amiga: Introduce a Friend
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Sol wants to meet your friends today! Grab a partner — a sibling, a stuffed animal, or a family member — for a pair-up game.
A friend who is a boy is [[el amigo]]. Point to your partner (if he's a boy) and say 'Mi amigo se llama... (his name)!'
A friend who is a girl is [[la amiga]]. Point to your partner (if she's a girl) and say 'Mi amiga se llama... (her name)!'
You introduced el amigo or la amiga to Sol using gestures and names — wonderful! Tomorrow is our biggest fiesta yet, mixing every word from two whole weeks!

questions.q: Grown-up, read aloud: 👦 Is this picture el niño or la niña?
Grown-up, read aloud: 👧 Is this picture el niño or la niña?
Grown-up, read aloud: Sol made a new friend who is a boy. Do we say el amigo or la amiga?
questions.explanation: ¡Sí! El amigo is a friend who is a boy.

questions.q: Grown-up, read aloud: Sol made a new friend who is a girl. Do we say el amigo or la amiga?
questions.explanation: ¡Sí! La amiga is a friend who is a girl.

objectives: Say el amigo (friend, male) or la amiga (friend, female) to describe a partner
Introduce a partner by name using 'Mi amigo/amiga se llama...' with gesture support
materialsNeeded: A partner for your child — a sibling, family member, or stuffed animal works fine
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Help your child choose a partner (a family member or a stuffed animal) for today's pair-up game.
2. Model it first with Sol: point to Sol and say 'Mi amigo se llama Sol!' (or 'mi amiga' if Sol is cast as a girl in your house — either works).
3. Have your child point to their partner and say 'Mi amigo se llama... (name)!' or 'Mi amiga se llama... (name)!' depending on the partner.
4. Swap partners 2-3 times so your child practices both el amigo and la amiga if possible.
5. Complete the on-screen multiple-choice activity together, reading each question aloud since your child may not read yet.
6. Close by asking: 'What do we call a friend who is a boy? A friend who is a girl?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: only one partner available today? That's perfectly fine — practice just el amigo or la amiga with that one partner, and add the other word another day
Ready for more: have your child introduce two or three different partners in a row, switching between el amigo and la amiga each time
Gesture support matters more than perfect grammar this week — a point plus 'amigo' or 'amiga' plus a name is a complete, successful introduction at this age
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken introduction activity — success looks like your child pointing to a partner and attempting 'mi amigo/amiga se llama... (name)', not a written answer. In the multiple-choice game: boy picture → el niño, girl picture → la niña, boy friend → el amigo, girl friend → la amiga.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Builds toward week 2's WA-WL-2015.1.1 Interpersonal Communication target by having the child introduce a third person (not just themselves), the natural next step after Day 1's self-introduction and Day 2's question-and-answer exchange, and recycles el niño/la niña from Day 3 in the multiple-choice review.
